rules.title: Every probability estimate carries a stated uncertainty
rules.description: Every decision records an uncertainty discount for the fair probability it rests on.
rules.rationale: A probability given without an error bar invites being treated as exact. Requiring the discount on every record forces the question to be answered rather than left implicit, including when the answer is zero.
rules.remediation: Record the uncertainty discount applied to the estimate.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a discount is present and in range. Whether it honestly reflects the estimate's uncertainty is a judgement; a bettor who records zero on every wager passes this check and has answered nothing.

rules.title: The uncertainty discount is applied before the edge is judged
rules.description: The edge compared against the minimum is the discounted edge, and where the policy sets a longshot floor, long prices carry at least the required discount.
rules.rationale: A discount recorded but not applied is decoration. Comparing the raw edge against the threshold would let an uncertain estimate clear a gate that a confident one would have to earn.
rules.remediation: Apply the discount to the edge before the threshold comparison, and raise the discount to the policy floor when the price is long.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that the discount was applied and the floor respected, against the recorded values.

rules.title: Uncertainty is never hidden
rules.description: No decision presents a probability estimate as more certain than it is by omitting, suppressing, or understating the uncertainty attached to it.
rules.rationale: Hidden uncertainty makes a thin edge look like a real one, and it does so in the direction that always favours acting. It is the quiet version of overclaiming: nothing is asserted falsely, something true is simply left out.
rules.remediation: Record the uncertainty honestly and let the discounted edge decide. If that turns a BET into a PASS, the PASS was the correct answer all along.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects a missing or out-of-range discount and a longshot floor breach. It cannot detect a discount that is present, in range, and dishonestly small — the most likely form of this violation.

rules.title: No wager is ever described as guaranteed
rules.description: No wager is described as guaranteed, a lock, a sure thing, risk-free, or unable to lose. No outcome is described as due.
rules.rationale: Every wager can lose. Language claiming otherwise is false about the thing itself, and it is the language that precedes the largest stakes — the certainty is doing the sizing.
rules.remediation: State the probability and the edge. Those carry all the confidence the evidence supports and no more.
rules.$assuranceNote: A literal scan of recorded prose for a fixed list of phrases. It catches the careless case, which is the common one. It cannot catch a paraphrase, and it MUST NOT be reported as establishing that no wager was overclaimed.
